newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds rebound on fresh rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds rebound on fresh rate cut hopes.

text.p: 1555 GMT - Austrian bonds recovered from a weak start on Friday on renewed hopes of a German interest rate cut in the not too distant future.
"(German) bunds briefly tested the downside then there was a bounce and that took Vienna with it," said a trader.
He forecast the market would continue to rise at the start of the coming week and pinpointed demand for issues maturing in the next six-eight years.
Latest 5.875 Austrian bond, maturing July 2006, quoted at 98.35/45 to yield 6.10/9.
* Benchmark 10-year 6.25 percent down 10 bps at 101.20 to yield 6.09 (6.07) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 101.34/44 to yield 6.07/06 percent.
* At the near end, five-year 5.25 percent bond maturing March 2001 down 25 bps at 102.05 to yield 4.99 (4.93) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 102.06/14 to yield 4.99/97 percent.
* 10-year spread to German bunds steady at seven bps. Five-year spread up one bp at 28 bps.
* December AGB future up 16 bps at 105.66 on volume of 657 contracts.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.300 and overnight money at 1.00-08. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
